topicName: Production Settings, Environment Variables, and WSGI/ASGI Servers (Gunicorn/Uvicorn)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Production Settings, Environment Variables, and WSGI/ASGI Servers in Django"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Moving a Django application from development to production requires hardening configurations, securing sensitive data using environment variables, and deploying robust application servers like Gunicorn or Uvicorn. This guide outlines industry-standard practices for setting up a production-ready Django environment."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Separating Production Settings"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"In development, Django relies on a single settings.py file containing insecure defaults. For production, you should split your settings into base, development, and production modules, or use environment variables to override default values dynamically."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"INSTALLED_APPS = [
    # ...
]

# SECURITY WARNING: don't run with debug turned on in production!
DEBUG = False

ALLOWED_HOSTS = ['yourdomain.com', 'www.yourdomain.com']

# Secure Database Configuration
DATABASES = {
    'default': {
        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',
        'NAME': 'production_db',
        'USER': 'db_user',
        'PASSWORD': 'secure_password',
        'HOST': 'localhost',
        'PORT': '5432',
    }
}"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Managing Environment Variables with python-decouple"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Never hardcode secrets like SECRET_KEY, database credentials, or API keys in your codebase. Use the python-decouple library to load these variables safely from an external .env file."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"pip install python-decouple"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Next, update your production settings to load variables securely:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"from decouple import config, Csv

SECRET_KEY = config('SECRET_KEY')
DEBUG = config('DEBUG', default=False, cast=bool)
ALLOWED_HOSTS = config('ALLOWED_HOSTS', cast=Csv())

DATABASES = {
    'default': {
        'ENGINE': 'django.db.backends.postgresql',
        'NAME': config('DB_NAME'),
        'USER': config('DB_USER'),
        'PASSWORD': config('DB_PASS'),
        'HOST': config('DB_HOST', default='localhost'),
        'PORT': config('DB_PORT', default='5432'),
    }
}"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Production Security Settings"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"Ensure your production settings include critical security headers and HTTPS enforcement parameters:"},{"order":13,"type":"code","text":"CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE = True
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE = True
SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT = True
SECURE_HSTS_SECONDS = 31536000
SECURE_HSTS_INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS = True
SECURE_HSTS_PRELOAD = True"},{"order":14,"type":"subheading","text":"4. WSGI vs. ASGI Servers"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"Django projects come with a wsgi.py file for synchronous applications and an asgi.py file if you are utilizing Django Channels or asynchronous views. In production, Django's built-in runserver command must not be used. Instead, you need a production-grade application server."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Gunicorn: A WSGI application server best suited for standard synchronous Django applications."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Uvicorn: An ASGI server built on uvloop and httptools, ideal if your Django project uses asynchronous features or WebSockets."},{"order":18,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Running Gunicorn for WSGI Apps"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install Gunicorn in your production environment and run it, pointing to your project's WSGI application module."},{"order":20,"type":"code","text":"pip install gunicorn
gunicorn myproject.wsgi:application --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 --workers 3"},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Running Uvicorn for ASGI Apps"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"If your project requires ASGI capabilities, use Uvicorn as your application server."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"pip install uvicorn[standard]
uvicorn myproject.asgi:application --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 --workers 4"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"7. Managing Servers with Systemd"},{"order":25,"type":"paragraph","text":"To ensure your Gunicorn or Uvicorn server restarts automatically on system boot or failure, configure a Systemd service file."},{"order":26,"type":"code","text":"[Unit]
Description=Gunicorn daemon for Django project
After=network.target

[Service]
User=www-data
Group=www-data
WorkingDirectory=/home/user/myproject
ExecStart=/home/user/myproject/env/bin/gunicorn --access-logfile - --workers 3 --bind unix:/home/user/myproject/myproject.sock myproject.wsgi:application

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target"},{"order":27,"type":"subheading","text":"Summary"},{"order":28,"type":"paragraph","text":"By keeping sensitive keys out of version control, enforcing strict security parameters, and deploying behind Gunicorn or Uvicorn managed by Systemd and Nginx, your Django application will be secure, scalable, and resilient in a production environment."}]
